bib.title: LongCLI-Bench: A Preliminary Benchmark and Study for Long-horizon Agentic Programming in Command-Line Interfaces

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "LongCLI-Bench: A Preliminary Benchmark and Study for Long-horizon Agentic Programming in Command-Line Interfaces", Yukang Feng, Jianwen Sun, Zelai Yang (equal contribution) et al. Preprint: the only venue marking is "arXiv:2602.14337v2 [cs.SE] 26 Feb 2026". First author's affiliations as printed: "NKU", "SII", "Shanda AI Research Tokyo" (abbreviations only).
File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/08-eval/sources/feng-2026-longcli-bench.pdf

COVERAGE: 11 of 11 pages, 49,133 of 49,133 chars. References (p9-11) skimmed. There is no appendix. Figure 3 (self-correction curves) is an image, so only the values repeated in prose or Table 4 were readable.

CLAIMS

1. Grading is two test sets plus a step score, and a pass is strict.
   - number: pass requires a 100% step score on both sets
   - setup: 20 tasks, Docker, tests run by the harness at completion or timeout
   - quote (p6): "A binary "pass" is defined strictly: a test set is considered passed only when its step score reaches 100%. ... The overall Pass Rate is defined as the percentage of tasks where the agent pass on both F2P and P2P tests."
   - The partial-credit metric is defined only as (p6) "the percentage of sub-steps completed". No formula or weighting is given. Sub-steps come from parsing a course's grading script, or from requirements manually segmented into sub-tasks (p5).
   - Task validity (p5): "A task is valid if the F2P tests fail on the initial repo and pass on the solution repo, while the P2P tests pass on both."
   - Tests are written from the requirement document, not the solution, and favour checking environment state (port listening, log content) (p4-5).

2. Headline pass rates are all below 20%.
   - number: best 16.7% (Claude Code with Opus-4.6 and with Opus-4.5); range 5.0-16.7%
   - setup: single-turn, unified system prompt, mean of 3 independent runs, 9 agent-model pairs
   - quote (p7, Table 2): "Claude-Opus-4.616.7 25.0 20.0 50.778.3 99.1 17.6" (columns: Pass, Pass@3, F2P Pass, F2P Step, P2P Pass, P2P Step, Time in min)
   - Other rows: GPT-5.3-Codex 15.0 / 20.0 / 18.3 / 44.1 / 86.7 / 99.5 / 8.8; OpenHands with DeepSeek-V3.1 5.0 / 10.0 / 11.7 / 25.3 / 88.3 / 99.7 / 17.9.

3. Failures concentrate early.
   - number: 38.3-65.0% of runs score in the [0,30) F2P band; only 5.0-15.0% fall in [80,100)
   - setup: Table 3, same runs
   - quote (p7): "Claude-Opus-4.6 38.3 20.0 10.0 11.7 20.0" and "DeepSeek-V3.1 65.0 13.3 5.0 5.0 11.7" (bands [0,30) [30,60) [60,80) [80,100) [100])
   - The abstract says "the majority of tasks stall at less than 30% completion", but this is a majority only for GPT-5.2-Codex (51.7) and the three OpenHands models. For the other five pairs it is the largest band, not a majority.

4. Regressions are hidden by the mean step score.
   - number: P2P step score above 98% for all pairs, P2P pass 70.0-88.3%
   - quote (p6): "While the average P2P step scores are very high (>98%) across all models, the P2P pass rate is notably lower, ranging from 70.0% to 88.3%."
   - The weakest agent has the best P2P pass (88.3%); the authors suggest it edits less.

5. Human collaboration and self-correction roughly triple the pass rate.
   - setup: Table 4, two pairs only. Plan is key plans injected before execution, with no code. Interactive is agent-requested guidance, capped at 3 interventions, with code requests denied.
   - quote (p8), Claude-Opus-4.6: "Base (Avg) 16.7 50.7 17.6 - / Self-Correction 55.0 63.6 43.8 - / Plan 58.3 65.4 15.4 - / Interactive 58.3 67.4 39.6 2.4 / Plan & Interactive 61.7 69.3 35.4 2.1" (Pass, F2P Score, Time in min, Inter.Avg)
   - GPT-5.3-Codex: Base 15.0, Self-Correction 40.0, Plan 41.7, Interactive 45.0, Plan & Interactive 50.0; times 8.8 / 26.7 / 10.7 / 25.9 / 22.4 min.
   - Plan matches or beats self-correction at well under half the time (15.4 vs 43.8 min for Claude; 10.7 vs 26.7 for Codex).
   - Self-correction can add regressions (p7): "Claude-Opus-4.6 reaches 95% at T2 but drops to 90% at T3" (P2P pass). GPT-5.3-Codex reaches 100% at T3.

6. Scale against Terminal-Bench@2.
   - quote (p6, Table 1): "Terminal-Bench@2 89 0.69 227.7 206.7 / LongCLI-Bench 20 104.0 15,000+ 1000+" (tasks, files, LoC, expert minutes)
   - Tasks were filtered from 958 assignments across 108 courses plus 50 real-world workflows. Each task took about 40 hours to build (p9).

7. Error analysis: 50 failed trajectories inspected by hand. Three causes are named (repetitive loops, environment misdiagnosis, long-run inconsistency and regression) with no counts per cause (p8-9).

LIMITS
- Authors concede (p9): a small dataset because of manual effort, and step scores "do not fully assess agent performance in areas like code quality or efficiency". The title says "Preliminary".
- Repeats: 3 runs, means only. There are no confidence intervals, variances or significance tests. With 20 tasks and 3 runs, one run is 1.67 points, so 16.7 vs 15.0 is one run out of 60. Pass@3 is reported but never defined.
- Cost: wall-clock minutes only. No tokens, dollars or step counts.
- "Early" is inferred from a low step score. The paper does not show that sub-steps are ordered or equally weighted, so a low score means few sub-steps passed, not a measured point in time.
- The self-correction rows read as multiples of 5 (40.0, 55.0), which would fit a single run, while the Plan rows (41.7, 58.3) fit 3 runs. The paper does not state the run count for Table 4 or which turn the self-correction row reports.
- Self-correction feeds test feedback back to the agent, so it is not comparable to a blind single-turn run. Human guidance was given by the authors' team, with no protocol or rater detail.
- Grading is outcome-only. Trajectories are inspected only in the manual error analysis.
- The contamination control (renaming identifiers and stories in course assignments) is asserted, not tested.
- The initial filter used Codex to discard easy tasks, which may bias the set against Codex-family agents. The paper does not discuss this.
- The prose contradicts its own table (p8): "Claude Code improved from 58.3% (Plan) to 58.3% (Interactive) in pass rate". Only the F2P score rose (65.4 to 67.4).
- Model names (Opus-4.6, GPT-5.3-Codex) date the numbers.

BUILDS ON: SWE-bench (Jimenez et al., 2024) for the F2P/P2P lineage. Terminal-Bench (Laude Institute, 2025) for the sandbox and as the comparison. OpenHands (Wang et al., 2024). Self-correction follows Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023) and Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2023). Contamination concerns cite Xu et al., 2024 and Deng et al., 2024.

CODE: none. Project page: https://github.com/finyorko/longcli-bench

FIGURES: one candidate, Figure 1, p2, "Task sample in LongCLI-Bench." It shows a single task with F2P at 80% and P2P at 90% step score yet "Pass: 0", which makes the gap between partial credit and the strict pass visible at a glance. Its text labels extract garbled, so check the rendered image. Table 3 on p7 is the stronger evidence for the early-failure claim, but it is a table.

PROBLEMS: no embedded instructions. Minor extraction faults: fused table cells ("Opus-4.616.7", "50.778.3", "25.388.3") and missing spaces around bold terms. Figure 3 data points are not recoverable from text.
